_purpose: Synthetic narrative text for REV | Narrative | Scrub Free-Text (WBS 5.3, 5.4). Same shape as scoring-test-data.json so provisioning/dataverse/seed-test-data.ps1 loads it with -DataPath. SYNTHETIC ONLY: every name, practice, address, phone number and email is invented. Phones are Ofcom drama ranges (07700 900xxx, 0113 496 0xxx); emails use example.org (narrative text) and example.invalid (applicant rows); postcodes are real districts with nobody attached. Nothing here comes from docs/Import/.
_neverProduction: These rows must never be loaded into PRD. All three test-data scripts refuse -Env prd.
_markup: `narratives` holds the gold standard per raw column: [[CATEGORY:text]] marks a span, as in src/tests/narrative/corpus/narratives.json. The plain text in `application` is that markup removed (test_narrative_test_data.py checks they agree). `expectedRedacted` is the redacted counterpart the rules require, written out from the gold spans; `null` means the flow must NOT write that counterpart.
_whoFindsWhat: PHONE and the postcode inside an ADDRESS are found by the flow's own shape rules (deterministic, a miss is a flow defect). NAME, FAMILY MEMBER, GP PRACTICE, EMAIL, AGE and the street part of an ADDRESS come from the AI Builder entity extraction model, so a miss there is model recall, which is what wbs:5.7 measures.
_scoring: src/tests/narrative/score_seeded_run.py compares the live counterparts with `expectedRedacted` and the live release flags with `expectedRecord`.

cases.purpose: Typical application: names, a family member, GP practice, address, phone, email and ages spread over six columns.
cases.proves: Every direct-identifier label is produced, an age lands in the right band, and a written record that passes every check is released when the process owner has switched auto-release on.

cases.purpose: Edge case: one narrative of about 10,400 characters (three windows) with identifiers inside the window overlap, a column with nothing to redact, a short column with identifiers, and eleven empty columns.
cases.proves: Windows and their overlap work (no ai-error), a column whose redacted text cannot fit 4,000 characters is held back and sent to review rather than truncated, an empty column is skipped, and a column with nothing to redact is copied through unchanged.
cases.expectedWindows: rev_narrativeraw is 10,456 characters: three windows at offsets 0, 4798 and 9596 (lengths 4998, 4998, 860). The phone and email sit in the 200-character overlap of windows 1 and 2, the second NAME starts at 4999 and is whole only in window 2.

_expectedRecord: `expectedRecord` is what the flow must write to rev_redactionreleased / rev_redactionreviewrequired, and the reason codes it must report to the process owner (Teams card), for each of the two settings states. The reasons are not stored on the row. TD-13's 'released: true' assumes the live extractor scores every name, practice, family member, age and email it redacts at 0.85 or more; a lower live score gives 'below-threshold' and is a finding about the model (wbs:5.7), not about the flow. The other cases do not depend on the model's scores.
